Task.
What family relation between Maya and Sara follows from the stated links? Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.

Problem 685. Reasoning across generations: case 5
Knowledge context.
Genealogies are relational graphs. Generation distance can be counted through parent links.
Given facts.

Maya is a parent of Noah. Noah is a parent of Lina. Maya is also a parent of Owen. Owen is a parent of Sara. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.

A parent is one generation above a child. A grandparent is two parent-links above. People who share a parent are siblings under this simplified model. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
What family relation between Lina and Sara follows from the stated links? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Noah and Owen are siblings because they share parent Maya. 2. Lina is child of Noah; Sara is child of Owen. 3. Children of siblings are cousins in this model. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
Answer.
Lina and Sara are cousins under the implied family tree. Cross-domain answer: 14:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
Family relations can be derived step by step from a small set of explicit links.
Formal model.
Directed parent graph; kinship predicates derived from path length and shared ancestors.
N13. Anachronisms and temporal compatibility
Problem 686. Temporal compatibility in a story set in 1400
Knowledge context.
Anachronism can be tested as a compatibility problem when the relevant date ranges are supplied.
Given facts.

For this problem, availability intervals are: Technology A: 1200–1600; Institution B: 1500–1900; Tool C: 1700–2000; Practice D: 1300–1450. A story is set in 1400 and mentions Technology A and Tool C together. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 10 members, requires at least 6 present for quorum, and 8 are present.
Rules.

An item is temporally compatible with a year only if the year lies inside its stated availability interval. An anachronism is an item placed outside its given interval. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Task.
Which mentioned item, if any, is anachronistic in the story? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Check 1400 against Technology A interval 1200–1600. 2. Check 1400 against Tool C interval 1700–2000. 3. Items outside their intervals: ['Tool C']. Cross-domain check: compare 8 with 6; 8≥6 is true.
Answer.
Anachronistic: Tool C. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
Knowledge takeaway.
The reasoning does not require memorizing invention dates if the intervals are part of the problem.
Formal model.
Interval membership test for each object-event pair.
Problem 687. Temporal compatibility in a story set in 1550
Knowledge context.
Anachronism can be tested as a compatibility problem when the relevant date ranges are supplied.
Given facts.

For this problem, availability intervals are: Technology A: 1200–1600; Institution B: 1500–1900; Tool C: 1700–2000; Practice D: 1300–1450. A story is set in 1550 and mentions Technology A and Tool C together. Cross-domain check: researchers collected 13 reports, but 4 are exact duplicate copies that add no new independent information.
Rules.

An item is temporally compatible with a year only if the year lies inside its stated availability interval. An anachronism is an item placed outside its given interval. For the cross-domain check, independent reports = total reports − duplicate copies.
Task.
Which mentioned item, if any, is anachronistic in the story? Cross-domain check: how many non-duplicate reports remain?
